Consult Summary:
- Patient presented with a 2–3 day history of increased shortness of breath, wheezing, and cough during exertion, unresponsive to salbutamol inhaler. 
- Asthma exacerbation suspected; instructed to increase preventer dose and seek GP review, with emergency advice if symptoms worsen.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Asthma exacerbation
- 2–3 day history of increased shortness of breath, wheezing, and cough, worse with exertion.
- Symptoms not relieved by salbutamol (blue inhaler), used as needed.
- No increased sputum production.
- No recent hospital admissions.
- Last asthma attack was 3–4 years ago; managed by continuing inhalers, never required oral steroids or antibiotics.
- Last asthma review was approximately 2 years ago.
- Previously well-controlled asthma.
- Typical peak flow reading when well: ~380 (units not specified).
- Family history: brother with asthma, sister with eczema.
- Management plan: increase Clenil (brown inhaler) to four puffs twice daily; continue salbutamol inhaler as needed every 2–4 hours; if symptoms worsen, attend A&E; arrange GP asthma review.

Issue 2: Possible eczema
- Mentions using Cetraben and hydrocortisone for skin symptoms, possibly eczema (self-described).
- No further details on severity or body sites given.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
- Patient reports having hay fever.
- No mention of acute flare, treatment, or associated symptoms.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented; "as needed" use described).
- Clenil (brown inhaler; currently three puffs twice daily, advised to increase to four puffs twice daily).
- Cetraben (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Hydrocortisone (topical; dose/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Hay fever.
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Possible eczema (not formally diagnosed).

Social History:
- Not discussed in transcript.

Preventative History:
- Last asthma review approximately 2 years ago.
- No mention of cervical screening test, mammogram, prostate blood test, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, vaccination status, skin check, or optometry.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed in this consult; plans made for future chest exam and peak flow assessment at GP visit.
- No vital signs recorded.

Plan:
- Increase Clenil (brown inhaler) dose to four puffs twice daily until reviewed.
- Use salbutamol inhaler up to every 2–4 hours as needed.
- Book face-to-face GP appointment for asthma review and chest examination.
- Advise immediate presentation to A&E if symptoms worsen before planned review.
- Possible need for antibiotics or oral steroids to be reassessed at in-person review.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements: 
- No social history, vitals, or full physical exam performed.
- Medication reconciliation incomplete (doses/frequencies/indications not fully documented).
- No details of vaccination status or general preventative history.
- No smoking or alcohol history documented.
- No specific eczema assessment.
●	Internal conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Good clarity; medication names repeated for confirmation; no major inaudible or noisy sections. Some incomplete details (e.g., inhaler brand clarification), but core clinical points intact.
